chief_complaint.title: Chief Complaint / Reason for Admission
chief_complaint.narrative: Acute severe right lower quadrant abdominal pain, low-grade fever (100.8°F), anorexia, nausea, and vomiting for 24 hours prior to presentation.

hospital_course.title: Hospital Course
hospital_course.narrative:
Hospital Day 1 (Admission & Surgery - 2023-09-10): Patient is a 34-year-old male who presented to the Emergency Department with a 24-hour history of periumbilical abdominal pain migrating to the right lower quadrant with guarding and rebound tenderness at McBurney's point. Vital signs on presentation were notable for temperature 38.2°C (100.8°F), heart rate 104 bpm, and BP 138/86 mmHg. Labs demonstrated leukocytosis with WBC 15.4 K/uL and 83% neutrophils. Contrast-enhanced CT scan of the abdomen/pelvis confirmed acute suppurative appendicitis with an obstructing appendicolith (8 mm) and localized pericecal fat stranding without frank abscess or pneumoperitoneum.
Patient was resuscitated with 2 Liters IV lactated Ringer's solution, initiated on IV Cefoxitin 2g, and consented for urgent surgery. Patient was taken to the operating room on 2023-09-10 at 14:30. A 3-port laparoscopic appendectomy was performed without complication. Operative findings confirmed an acutely inflamed, gangrenous, non-perforated retrocecal appendix with mesoappendix vascular engorgement. Hemostasis was meticulous; estimated blood loss was < 15 mL. Patient was extubated and transferred to the PACU in stable condition, then admitted to the 7th floor surgical floor.
Hospital Day 2 (Post-op Day 1 - 2023-09-11): Postoperative course was uncomplicated. Patient was ambulating in the hallways. Bowel sounds returned and flatus was passed in the afternoon. Diet was advanced from clear liquids to a soft surgical diet, which was well-tolerated without nausea. Pain was effectively controlled with oral acetaminophen and scheduled ibuprofen. Incisions were clean and dry.
Hospital Day 3 (Discharge Day - 2023-09-12): Patient is afebrile with normal vital signs (BP 118/74 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, temp 37.0°C). Surgical port sites are intact, clean, without erythema, hematoma, or discharge. Tolerating regular diet, voiding spontaneously, and ambulating independently. Patient is discharged home in stable condition with clear instructions for outpatient follow-up.

hospital_discharge_instructions.title: Discharge Instructions, Plan of Care & Follow-up
hospital_discharge_instructions.narrative:
• Activity Restrictions: No heavy lifting greater than 10 lbs, strenuous cardiovascular exercise, or core abdominal straining for 2 weeks. May walk and climb stairs at a comfortable pace.
• Bathing & Incision Care: Incisions have Dermabond / Steri-strips in place. May shower starting 48 hours post-op (gently pat dry). Do NOT soak in a bath, hot tub, or swim until evaluated at post-op visit.
• Dietary Guidance: Resume regular diet as tolerated. Maintain generous fluid hydration (at least 6-8 glasses of water daily) and high-fiber foods to avoid constipation while taking pain medications.
• Scheduled Follow-Up Appointments:
                
                  Postoperative Surgical Clinic visit with Dr. Sarah Jenkins on 2023-09-22 at 10:30 AM (Phone: 212-555-7010, 420 East 70th St, Suite 500).
                  Primary Care follow-up with Dr. Emily Watson on 2023-10-05 at 02:00 PM for routine blood pressure check and medication review.
• Red Flag Warning Symptoms: Call the surgical clinic immediately (212-555-7000) or report to the nearest emergency department if you experience:
                
                  Temperature > 101.0 °F (38.3 °C) or persistent chills
                  Severe or worsening abdominal pain not relieved by medications
                  Persistent nausea, vomiting, or inability to keep fluids down
                  Increasing redness, swelling, warmth, or purulent drainage around port incisions
                  Shortness of breath, chest pain, or lower extremity swelling
